inputs.share_count_basis: ADS-EQUIVALENT units so per-share outputs are per ADS, comparable to the Nasdaq quote. 435.9m equity shares issued at 31 Mar 2026 (issued capital INR 4,359m at INR 10 par; FY2026 weighted diluted 434.75m) plus ~0.3m option dilution = ~436.2m equity shares, divided by 6 (1 ADS = 6 equity shares since 4 Oct 2024) = 72.7m ADS-equivalents. There is no Indian listing; the ADS is the only traded line. Held flat: SBC is expensed in the flows. The 2024 rights issue (190.3m shares, 1.36364-for-1) is already in the count. A further equity raise to fund the capex gap is NOT modelled and is a downside risk to the per-ADS value.
inputs.net_debt_note: Company-defined net debt at 30 Sep 2026 (Q2 FY2027 release): long-term borrowings 36,109 + short-term 18,572 = 54,681, less cash and bank 5,868 and deposits lien-marked to loans 3,482 = 45,331. Borrowings only; lease liabilities (3,902 at Mar 2026) are excluded because leases are charged in the flows (treatment B). Kotak CCD-related liabilities are not in borrowings and are handled through the NCI bridge item.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 20-F cash flow statement 'Stock compensation expense' INR 56m; no equity-award withholding taxes disclosed. Interest income not stripped (company is heavily net debt).
inputs.fx_note: Flows and statements in INR millions; quote is USD per ADS on Nasdaq. USD/INR 94.24 (Yahoo INR=X, 2026-11-15 03:30Z), so fx_rate (INR -> USD) = 1/94.24 = 0.010611. Per-ADS conversion is carried by the share count (ADS-equivalents = equity shares / 6), not by the fx rate. No dual listing exists for a parity check (equity shares are unlisted in India); the market-cap tie is 72.7m ADS x quote = ~USD 0.92bn = ~INR 86bn, consistent with the ~USD 1bn cap cited in the qualitative research. refresh_price moves the price but not this rate.
inputs.wacc_rationale: INR-built. Risk-free ~6.6% (India 10y G-sec), India equity risk premium ~7.2% (mature ERP plus country premium). Asset beta ~0.7 (contracted digital infrastructure plus enterprise connectivity), relevered at market D/E ~0.64 to ~1.04 -> cost of equity ~14.1%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~9.5% (FY2026 interest on borrowings 3,614 on ~37bn average borrowings; SISL rated ICRA AA) -> 7.1% after 25.17% tax. Market weights ~61% equity / 39% debt -> ~11.4%, rounded to 11.5%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: leverage, funding and lease-up risk are carried in the scenario flows and weights, not in a stacked premium. Terminal growth 5.0% nominal INR (about 4% inflation plus ~1% real), below the risk-free rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment B (leases as operating cost). Lease cash (principal 429 + interest 336 = 765 in FY2026, 1.7% of revenue) is charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities (3,902) are excluded from net debt. D&A path is ex right-of-use depreciation (FY2026 D&A 7,274 less ROU depreciation 905 = 6,369, 14.2% of revenue). Capex path includes the 'amount paid for acquisition of right-of-use assets' (IRU/land prepayments, 934 in FY2026) that sits in investing outside the PP&E line.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are 100% consolidated; Kotak funds (KSSF, KDCF) own 11.55% of data-center subsidiary Sify Infinit Spaces (SISL) after the Feb 2026 CCD conversion. Because of put-option accounting the consolidated NCI line is nil, so the stake is deducted once in the equity bridge at INR 10,658m, the NCI the 20-F (note 18A) says arises on termination of the subscription agreements (3,406 'other equity interest' + 6,063 liabilities + pre-conversion share 1,200 less 11 of losses). That is roughly the Kotak cost (~10bn) and close to 11.55% of the SISL equity value the base case implies; at the IPO investor bid (INR 220-250bn for SISL) the stake would be 25-29bn, but the listed price of the whole group does not support that mark.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF with non-US adaptations (INR flows, USD ADS quote, leases, NCI). Sify is an operating company (network, data-center colocation, digital services), not a REIT: it pays tax, does not distribute, and its value is the unlevered cash flow of a capacity build-out, so AFFO/NAV routes do not apply. PHILOSOPHY: neither latest FCF (negative: -4.8bn in FY2026 and roughly -20bn annualised in H1 FY2027 on capex of ~INR 8.6bn in Q2 alone) nor a mid-cycle average is usable; the build explicitly models the capex cycle - capex at 55% of revenue in FY2027 fading to 14% by FY2036 - and the revenue and margin that capacity earns, on a 10-year horizon so the terminal year is post-build. The decisive judgment is the return on the build: observed economics are roughly INR 500m of capex per MW against ~INR 155m revenue per operational MW at ~44% data-center segment margin, a ~14-15% EBITDA yield on cost, against an 11.5% INR WACC. That is thin value creation, and the existing capital base earns ~5% pre-tax (operating profit ~4.6bn annualised on ~75bn net invested capital, part of which is not-yet-earning work in progress). The DCF therefore values the enterprise near its invested capital, well below the market's ~1.9x. CROSS-CHECK (memo, not in the value): market EV ~131bn net debt-inclusive plus NCI and leases is ~11.7x annualised H1 FY2027 adjusted EBITDA; base-case EV is a low-to-mid single-digit multiple, at or below where the ADS traded before the 2024-26 data-center re-rating, during a period when a large share of capital is not yet earning. Reported FCF (OCF less PP&E purchases) is pre-interest because finance costs are classified in financing; it also excludes 765 of lease cash and 934 of ROU prepayments, both charged in the forward flows. FY2027 growth 21.5% is anchored on H1 FY2027 revenue of 26,150 (+23% YoY); no numeric guidance is issued. Working capital: growth consumes cash (FY2026 working-capital outflow 2.6bn on 5bn revenue growth; FY2025 inflow), modelled at -10% of incremental revenue. Tax: Indian statutory 25.17% on unlevered EBIT, never credited on a loss; cash taxes paid were 650-1,285 a year even through the loss years (withholding and profitable entities). Price is a regular-session close, not an after-hours print.

equity_bridge.item: Kotak funds' 11.55% stake in Sify Infinit Spaces (NCI on termination of DSA)
equity_bridge.note: FY2026 20-F note 18A (iv); deducted once here, flows are 100% consolidated

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_10yr_cagr (FY2016-FY2026 11.6%); base path compounds at 11.7% over ten years
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (3.4% / 7.5%) is far below revenue CAGR (10.3% / 13.0%) and is flattered by the 2024 rights issue (INR 2.5bn) while FY2025-26 losses eroded it; equity CAGR is not a usable growth anchor here. EPS is negative in FY2025-26 and owner FCF is negative in five of the last eight years, so EPS and FCF CAGRs are undefined.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF series (reported FCF less SBC; no interest strip) FY2019-FY2026: -2,532, 593, 3,964, -4,913, -3,712, -5,195, -2,449, -4,836. SBC is immaterial (under 0.2% of revenue throughout).

base.margin_note: Terminal 32% is a segment-mix build: data center ~55% of FY2036 revenue at ~45% segment margin, network ~33% at ~17%, digital ~12% at ~2%, less support costs, plus SG&A leverage (SG&A was flat YoY in Q2 FY2027 on +31% revenue).
base.capex_note: FY2027 55% of revenue (~INR 30bn) from H1 run-rate: net debt rose 13.9bn in six months and Q2 capex alone was 8.6bn. Fade assumes the 113 MW contracted backlog and ~150 MW under construction are delivered by FY2029-30, then growth capex slows; terminal 14% is ~8% maintenance plus growth capex for 5% nominal growth.

bear.capex_note: Uncommitted build is curtailed once lease-up disappoints: after the backlog is delivered capex falls to ~maintenance plus the little growth a 5% nominal path needs.

scenario_narratives.base: The 113 MW contracted backlog and most of the ~150 MW under construction are delivered by FY2029-30 at roughly today's economics (about INR 500m capex and ~INR 155m revenue per MW, ~44-45% data-center segment margin). Revenue compounds 11.7% a year to ~INR 135bn in FY2036, in line with the FY2016-26 record, with data center rising to over half the mix; network grows high single digits on thin, renewal-compressed margins; digital stops shrinking but earns almost nothing. Adjusted EBITDA margin climbs from 23.5% to 32% on mix and SG&A leverage. Capex stays above 25% of revenue through FY2030, so free cash flow is negative for about four more years and the build is funded by more debt; the SISL IPO is not assumed. The build earns roughly its cost of capital, not a multiple of it.
scenario_narratives.bull: India's AI/hyperscale capacity shortage persists: Sify leases new capacity as fast as it can energise it, at firm pricing with escalators, and wins further GPU-cloud and hyperscaler campuses in Mumbai, Chennai and Noida. Revenue compounds ~14% to ~INR 165bn, the data-center mix and operating leverage take EBITDA margin to 36%, and each rupee of capex earns more revenue than today. A SISL listing at a favourable mark would add balance-sheet relief on top, but is not needed for these flows and is not valued separately.
scenario_narratives.bear: Jio, Airtel/Nxtra, Adani, NTT and STT GDC bring capacity on together and the market tips into oversupply just as Sify's debt-funded capacity lands: the backlog is delivered but lease-up beyond it is slow and renewal pricing softens, while network pricing keeps compressing and digital keeps shrinking. Growth fades to 5-6% after FY2028, margin stalls at 26%, and the capacity already paid for earns well below its cost of capital. With net debt above INR 45bn, INR 18.6bn of it short-term, and the IPO shelved, the equity is at the mercy of refinancing or a dilutive raise; the value to ordinary holders on this path is nil.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 30%: free cash flow is deeply negative, net debt rose 58% in a year to ~3.7x annualised EBITDA with a third of borrowings short-term, the deleveraging IPO is shelved, and every better-capitalised rival is adding capacity into the same market. Base 50%: the contracted backlog makes the next two to three years of revenue unusually visible. Bull cut to 20%: it needs sustained scarcity pricing, flawless delivery and continued cheap funding at the same time.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Explicit capex-cycle DCF, not latest or mid-cycle FCF: ten years of modelled build-out and lease-up, capitalised only once capex has fallen to a sustaining level. Risk is charged once, in the scenario flows and a bear-heavy weighting, with one INR-built 11.5% WACC. The valuation is dominated by the terminal value net of four more years of cash burn and a debt stack that is roughly a third of enterprise value at the market price; small changes in margin, capex productivity or discount rate move the equity value by multiples, so the per-ADS figures should be read as a range around a thin equity cushion rather than as a point estimate. The market price embeds returns on the data-center build well above what the company's reported economics show so far.
valuation_philosophy.limited_liability_note: The bear case produces a NEGATIVE equity value (enterprise value ~INR 40bn against ~INR 56bn of net debt and NCI): on that path the ADS is worth nil, not less than nil. The engine does not floor per-share values, so the weighted IV carries the negative bear figure and is the more conservative reading; with the bear floored at zero the weighted value is ~USD 3.74 per ADS rather than ~USD 3.05. Hurdle entry prices are negative in bear and base: no price returns 15% on those paths. band_position is not meaningful here - SBC is ~0.1% of revenue, so house and street values nearly coincide and the ratio is degenerate.
key_risks_to_valuation: Discount rate: an infrastructure buyer underwriting contracted hyperscale capacity at 9.5-10% rather than 11.5% would pay far more; the sensitivity grid shows how steep this is
Return on the build: revenue and EBITDA per MW on the backlog are not disclosed; the model infers ~14-15% EBITDA yield on cost from consolidated figures
Funding: four more years of negative FCF must be borrowed or raised; a dilutive equity raise or a SISL sell-down at a low mark is not in the share count
SISL IPO: a listing near the investor bid (INR 220-250bn) would mark Sify's 88.45% stake above the entire current market capitalisation - upside the DCF does not credit
NCI: Kotak's 11.55% of SISL is deducted at ~INR 10.7bn; at IPO-type marks it would be 25-29bn
FX: INR flows against a USD quote; the rupee has depreciated steadily and the bridge rate is a spot rate
Balance-sheet vintage: net debt is September 2026, share count and lease/NCI figures are March 2026
